definition: Mathematics and AI refers to the two-way relationship between mathematics and artificial intelligence.
details: The two fields have been interrelated since the initial development of AI decades ago. On one hand, mathematics plays a key role in artificial intelligence. For example, many AI algorithms use methods relying on optimization, statistics and linear algebra. On the other hand, researchers have for decades been trying to use AI and computers to help solve mathematics problems. Artificial intelligence has made a significant impact on many academic disciplines. The impact has been pronounced in mathematics, where results are exactly verifiable.

explainer.lead: Mathematics and AI describes the two-way relationship between the fields: maths underpins AI algorithms, and AI is used to attack maths problems. The AI side has had a pronounced impact on mathematics because results there are exactly verifiable.

tiers.eli5: Maths is the toolkit that makes AI work, and AI in turn is being used as a helper for doing maths.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on optimisation, statistics and linear algebra as the algorithmic core. The pitfall is expecting AI-generated maths to be right — its value here rests on the fact that results can be checked exactly.
tiers.paperLevel: AI algorithms draw on optimisation, statistics and linear algebra; separately, AI and computers are applied to solving mathematics problems, a field where results are exactly verifiable.

explainer.example: A proof assistant combined with an AI model proposes a lemma; correctness is settled mechanically rather than by trusting the model.
